You are working on the Nxeon hosting platform at /opt/nxeon-staging (Next.js/TypeScript/Prisma/Postgres).

CRITICAL RULES:
- NEVER run `npm run build` in /opt/nxeon or /opt/nxeon-staging
- NEVER use `git add -A` or `git add .`
- Work only in /opt/nxeon-staging

## Task: Build Public Minecraft Server Directory

The schema already has these fields on the Server model:
- `publicListing Boolean @default(false)`
- `publicDescription String?`

### What to build:

**1. Server actions** — Add to `/opt/nxeon-staging/lib/actions-game-control.ts`:
- `togglePublicListing(serverId: string, enabled: boolean)` — requires server ownership. Sets publicListing.
- `updatePublicDescription(serverId: string, description: string)` — requires server ownership. Max 500 chars. Sets publicDescription.

**2. Game panel settings** — Add a "Public Directory" section to the game panel. Read `/opt/nxeon-staging/components/customer/gamepanel/GameServerPanel.tsx` to understand the structure. The settings tab already renders a `settingsPanel` prop from the parent page. 

Instead of modifying the settings panel (which is a prop), create a new component `/opt/nxeon-staging/components/customer/gamepanel/GamePublicListing.tsx` and render it in the Overview tab (GameOverview) or as a card within the settings. Actually, the cleanest approach: add it as a section in the Overview tab. Read `/opt/nxeon-staging/components/customer/gamepanel/GameOverview.tsx` to see the overview structure, then add a "Public Directory" card at the bottom.

The card should have:
- Toggle switch to enable/disable public listing
- Text area for public description (when enabled)
- Preview of how the listing will look
- Save button

If the overview is too crowded, create a standalone component and add it to the settings tab rendering in the server page. Read `/opt/nxeon-staging/app/dashboard/servers/[id]/page.tsx` around line 994 where `gameSettingsPanel` is constructed to add it there.

**3. Public directory page** — Create `/opt/nxeon-staging/app/game-servers/directory/page.tsx`:
- Server-rendered page showing all Minecraft servers with publicListing=true
- Each server card shows:
  - Server name (server.label || server.name)  
  - Public description
  - Player count (online/max from gamePlan.slots)
  - Connect address (subdomain.play.nxeon.cloud or ip:port)
  - Game variant/version badge
  - A "Copy address" button
- Sort by player count (most popular first), then by name
- Search/filter by name
- SEO: proper meta title "Public Minecraft Servers | Nxeon", description
- Match the Nxeon marketing page style (dark theme, gradient backgrounds). Look at other marketing pages in `/opt/nxeon-staging/app/(marketing)/` for the layout pattern — they use a shared layout with nav/footer.

**4. Link to directory** — Add a link to the public directory from the game servers marketing page. Check if `/opt/nxeon-staging/app/(marketing)/game-servers/page.tsx` or similar exists and add a "Browse Public Servers" CTA section.

Also add a link in the customer dashboard sidebar. Read the sidebar component to find where nav links are defined and add "Server Directory" under an appropriate section.

### Privacy guardrails:
- NEVER expose: server IP addresses (show subdomain or "Copy to connect" only), owner usernames/emails, internal server IDs, node names, VM IDs
- Only show: server name, description, player count, connect string (subdomain preferred), game variant
- The connect address shown should prefer subdomain over raw IP

### Style:
- Marketing pages: dark gradient background, large rounded cards, brand-500 purple accents
- Dashboard components: navy-900 bg, rounded-2xl cards, border-white/[0.06]

Run `npx tsc --noEmit` when done to verify no type errors. Do NOT touch the schema — it's already pushed.

- design: Create a design canvas — a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces — posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including Markdown ones — format is part of the design pass, never a speed shortcut.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, handing the viewer a file to save, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

2341	model FreeMinecraftServer {
2342	  id            String   @id @default(cuid())
2343	  userId        String   @unique
2344	  user          User     @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
2345	  // Public-facing name: reachable at `<subdomain>.<free_minecraft_domain>`.
2346	  // Validated against SUBDOMAIN_RE (lib/actions-free-minecraft.ts) at creation —
2347	  // lowercase alnum/hyphen, 3-20 chars — the same shape a DNS label allows.
2348	  subdomain     String   @unique
2349	  // The actual `docker run --name` on freemc-host; derived from `id` (not
2350	  // `subdomain`) so a container is never renamed if a future feature lets a
2351	  // player change their subdomain — the container identity and the public name
2352	  // are deliberately decoupled.
2353	  containerName String   @unique
2354	  // CREATING: DB row exists, docker run hasn't been confirmed yet (worker job
2355	  // pending/running). READY: container exists on the host — mc-router owns
2356	  // whether it's actually awake or asleep at any given moment; we don't mirror
2357	  // that live state here to avoid it going stale. DELETING/DELETED: teardown
2358	  // requested/complete.
2359	  status        String   @default("CREATING")
2360	  // Cosmetic display name shown in the dashboard — defaults to the subdomain,
2361	  // distinct from it so renaming never touches the connect address or the
2362	  // container's mc-router label.
2363	  name          String?
2364	  // DEPRECATED — kept only for backward compatibility with the legacy
2365	  // dashboard UI (components/customer/freemc/*.tsx) that still reads a flat
2366	  // "preset" instead of the two-axis gameType/gameMode model below (that UI
2367	  // is being replaced in a parallel change; do not build anything new
2368	  // against this field). Mirrors activeGameType, EXCEPT when activeGameType
2369	  // is "vanilla" and activeGameMode isn't "survival" — then it mirrors
2370	  // activeGameMode instead (creative/hardcore/peaceful), matching the exact
2371	  // flat keys the old FREEMC_PRESETS map used, so legacy cards still
2372	  // highlight the right entry. See legacyPresetKeyFor() in
2373	  // lib/free-minecraft-control.ts, the single place that computes it.
2374	  preset        String   @default("vanilla")
2375	  // Which FREEMC_GAME_TYPES key (lib/free-minecraft-control.ts) has an
2376	  // ISOLATED, persistent world currently loaded on this server's container —
2377	  // drives the itzg `LEVEL` env var at container-recreate time, so each game
2378	  // type's world lives in its own `<LEVEL>`/`<LEVEL>_nether`/`<LEVEL>_the_end`
2379	  // folder set inside the SAME /data volume mount and switching types never
2380	  // touches another type's saved world again (fixes the 2026-08-25 incident
2381	  // where a SkyBlock->Vanilla switch corrupted the one shared world — see
2382	  // lib/actions-freemc-worlds.ts). One FreeMinecraftWorld row exists per
2383	  // game type this account has ever actually visited.
2384	  activeGameType String  @default("vanilla")
2385	  // Which FREEMC_GAME_MODES key (survival/hardcore/creative/peaceful) is
2386	  // layered on top of activeGameType's world as a server.properties overlay
2387	  // (gamemode/hardcore/difficulty). Applied via RCON + a restart of the SAME
2388	  // container — never a world switch, never touches activeGameType's data.
2389	  activeGameMode String  @default("survival")
2390	  // One row per game type this account has ever applied (created lazily on
2391	  // first visit, NOT pre-created for all 9 types) — powers the world list
2392	  // (list/rename/last-played) in the dashboard. See
2393	  // lib/actions-freemc-worlds.ts.
2394	  worlds        FreeMinecraftWorld[]
2395	  createdAt     DateTime @default(now())

Everything is in place. Here is a summary of what was built.

---

**Summary: Public Minecraft Server Directory**

**1. Server actions** (`/opt/nxeon-staging/lib/actions-game-control.ts`):
- `togglePublicListing(serverId, enabled)` -- ownership-guarded toggle that sets `publicListing` on the Server model and revalidates both the directory page and the server's dashboard page.
- `updatePublicDescription(serverId, description)` -- ownership-guarded setter, max 500 chars, trims and nullifies empty strings.
- `getPublicListingState(serverId)` -- reads the current `publicListing` and `publicDescription` for the owner's panel UI.

**2. Game panel settings card** (`/opt/nxeon-staging/components/customer/gamepanel/GamePublicListing.tsx`):
- New `GamePublicListing` component rendered at the bottom of the game-panel Settings tab (added in `/opt/nxeon-staging/app/dashboard/servers/[id]/page.tsx` after `SftpAccess`).
- Toggle switch to enable/disable public listing.
- Textarea for public description (shown when enabled), 500-char limit with character counter.
- Live preview card showing how the listing will appear in the directory.
- Save button with feedback messages.

**3. Public directory page** (`/opt/nxeon-staging/app/(marketing)/game-servers/directory/page.tsx` + `DirectoryList.tsx`):
- Server-rendered page under the marketing layout (gets nav/footer automatically).
- Queries both paid `Server` (with `publicListing=true`, `status=RUNNING`) and free `FreeMinecraftServer` (with `isPublic=true`, `status=READY`).
- Privacy guardrails: only servers with a subdomain are shown (never raw IP); no internal IDs, owner info, node names, or VM IDs are exposed. React keys use truncated opaque prefixes (`p-` / `f-`).
- Each card shows: server name, description, player slots, game label/variant badge, free badge, connect address with copy button.
- Client-side search/filter by name, description, game label, or variant.
- SEO metadata: title "Public Minecraft Servers | Nxeon", proper description, canonical URL.
- CTA at the bottom promoting free server hosting.

**4. Directory links**:
- **Marketing page** (`/opt/nxeon-staging/app/(marketing)/game-servers/page.tsx`): "Browse Public Servers" CTA section added before the "Popular game servers" section, with a gradient card and link to `/game-servers/directory`.
- **Dashboard sidebar** (`/opt/nxeon-staging/app/dashboard/layout.tsx`): "Server Directory" nav link added under the Compute section, between "Game Servers" and "Volumes", linking to `/game-servers/directory`.
